title: Early Impact Canvas - New Hire Engineering Mentor Map
summary: Lightweight, engineer-facing canvas to set clear 30/60/90 impact goals, align mentor/peer expectations, and provide a short weekly sprint plan for the first eight weeks. Designed to be used in offer-to-day-1 comms and during week-1 kickoff with mentor + manager.
content:
Purpose:
- Create a single-page, pragmatic plan that reduces ambiguity for new ICs (IC2-IC4) in engineering teams. Focus on early wins, dependency mapping, and mentor deliverables.

How to use:
- Fill during offer acceptance or first 2 workdays with hiring manager + mentor.
- Save as: Team/Onboard/[role]-[name]-early-impact-canvas.md in the team's drive.
- Review every week for the first 8 weeks; manager + mentor sign-off at weeks 2, 4, and 8.

Sections (fillable prompts):
1) Role and immediate context (1-2 lines)
   - Example: "Platform infra, area: request routing. Team: inference-runtime. Reports to: Tom Nguyen."

2) 30/60/90 Impact goals (explicit, measurable)
   - 30d (stability + learning): "Ship a small observability delta: add endpoint metrics to /v1/requests; create runbook draft for one regularly failing route."
   - 60d (ownership + contribution): "Own a minor rollout: implement canary config and run two controlled experiments; reduce p95 latency tail by instrumentation-driven changes on a single model route."
   - 90d (independent delivery + cross-team): "Lead a small refactor to move a caching layer into shared lib and produce cost/latency before/after report; present to runtime guild."

3) Must-have onboarding tasks (first 14 days) - checklist
   - [ ] Get laptop + credentials + VPN & KMS access
   - [ ] Local dev environment: repo clones, build, run minimal inference example
   - [ ] Meet mentor + primary cross-team contacts (15m intros): SRE, infra, product owner
   - [ ] Complete security & infra runbook read (link)
   - [ ] Shadow a production incident review (watch or attend)

4) Mentor commitments (explicit deliverables & cadence)
   - Week 0-2: 1hr/day for pairing and quick context walkthroughs (architecture map, key repos)
   - Week 3-4: 3x30m sessions focused on feature flow and testing practices
   - Ongoing: weekly 60m sync + ad-hoc pairing up to 2hrs/week until week 8
   - Deliverables: annotated architecture doc, onboarding lab task, code review checklist tailored to new hire

5) Dependencies & blockers to resolve early
   - Typical blockers: KMS roles, dedicated GPU access in sandbox, service token access.
   - Delegate owner and ETA for each blocker.

6) Quick interview-readiness rubric (used for shadowing or future internal hiring):
   - System design (early-stage): Can the IC map the inference request flow and identify lat/loss points? (scale: 1-4)
   - Debugging: Reproduces a flaky failure locally or narrows down root cause in triage notes (1-4)
   - Code quality: Writes a concise, test-covered small PR with clear description and rollout plan (1-4)
   - Collaboration: Communicates blockers and escalations clearly with owner attribution (1-4)
   - Notes: This rubric is intentionally lightweight and meant for internal calibration, not an external hiring scorecard.

7) Week-by-week sprint sketch (first 8 weeks)
   - Week 0 (pre-boarding): admin, account setup, read-ahead links, architecture primers
   - Week 1: small lab task (end-to-end), first PR review, meet cross-functional partners
   - Week 2: finish a small bugfix or telemetry task, join daily standups as speaker for a status update
   - Week 3: tackle a small feature under mentor pairing, introduce test harnesses used by team
   - Week 4: shipping readiness: write rollout plan and automated smoke tests
   - Week 5-6: own a canary rollout with mentor oversight, produce metrics snapshot
   - Week 7-8: propose and land a small refactor or optimization, present outcome in team demo

8) Communication plan and escalation path
   - Daily: asynchronous status in onboarding channel (Slack) + weekly summary to manager
   - Blocker escalation: tag mentor -> team lead -> SRE on-call.

9) Success signals and expected artifacts by week 8
   - Deployed PR with observability and rollback plan
   - Runbook or architecture note authored or substantially edited by new hire
   - 1-2 short presentations: 'what I learned' and 'impact report'

10) Notes to self / loose ideas (working doc style)
   - Make the mentor deliverables explicit to avoid ad-hoc promises.
   - Consider a "sandbox day" where new hire can experiment without permissions constraints.
   - Track time-to-first-meaningful-PR as a metric for team onboarding health.

Appendix: sample mentor message (copyable)
Hi <Name>, excited to be your mentor. For the first two weeks we'll pair on setup and one lab task. I'll post a 30/60/90 stub by the end of week 1 and we'll iterate. Bring any questions to our weekly sync or ping me in #onboard-inference.

Quick links (placeholders)
- Team architecture doc: CONFLUENCE-ARCH-2024
- Sandbox provisioning guide: CONFLUENCE-SANDBOX-101
- Onboarding checklist template repo: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-templates

Feedback log (for manager/people ops to fill):
- Week 2 notes: ___________________________________________
- Week 4 notes: ___________________________________________
- Week 8 post-mortem: ___________________________________

End of canvas. Keep this document lean and actionable; copy into an OKR or personal sprint board if the hire needs more structure.
